idiom_name: SwiftNIO EventLoopGroup / SelectableEventLoop over kqueue or epoll
implementation_notes: SwiftNIO is the library realization: its documentation describes the event loop as the basic I/O primitive that waits for events (usually I/O related, such as data received) and fires a callback when they happen, MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup as a group that creates threads and places one SelectableEventLoop on each - a selector over kqueue or epoll that manages I/O events from file descriptors and dispatches work - and stresses that essentially all work must be dispatched through an EventLoop for thread safety. What replaces the classic structure is the ChannelPipeline: handlers are ChannelHandler objects attached to a channel, and futures or async-await express the completion of dispatched work. Without NIO the manual path is a DispatchSource readability source per descriptor; Swift's structured concurrency alone does not multiplex readiness.
pitfalls: Blocking work must never run on an event loop thread: the loop serves every channel assigned to it, so slow work goes through eventLoop.submit or an offloading thread pool.
NIO types are not thread-safe; touching a Channel or its pipeline from another thread without executing on its EventLoop trips NIO's precondition checks and races the dispatch.
Promises and handlers must be completed or removed deterministically: a promise never fulfilled leaves futures pending forever, and a handler retained after channel close leaks its resources.
